prompts.painterly_bark_v3_calm.png: Edit this game bark albedo tile into a substantially calmer hand-painted cartoon oak bark master texture. Flat square seamless repeating texture, NOT a tree or scene. Keep its restrained chestnut warm brown family and vertical flow, but eliminate at least 75 percent of the small thin internal streaks. Across the entire width show only 4 or 5 broad softly irregular vertical bark ribbons and at most 3 main narrow dark cracks, with occasional short splits. Most of the surface must be broad quiet almost uniform brush-painted colour areas, crisp deliberate edges of broad strokes rather than blur. Moderate low contrast. No photorealism, no tiny scratches, no fibres, no micrograin, no knots, no bevel or directional illumination baked into it, no highlights, no AO shadows, no text. Wrap match opposite edges both horizontally and vertically; cracks continue sensibly over vertical tile seams. This is an albedo-only game asset; coarse few hand-painted strokes matter more than details. Preserve handmade cartoon elegance while drastically simplifying texture frequency.

NOT a picture of a tree, not a scene, no branches, no bark, no sky, no perspective. Full coverage canvas of calm moss and sage green foliage paint. Make broad deliberately grouped leaf-like gouache brush shapes, some softly overlapping groups; 8 to 12 main broad irregular patches across the square with quiet unified background areas between. Each group is a few simple rounded or tapered expressive brush strokes, NOT dozens of individual leaves. Low contrast restrained earthy greens, muted olive and sage, subtle cooler dark green patches, modest warmer pale green areas. Distinct painted stroke edges, no blurry cloud gradients, no photorealism, no leaf veins, no speckling, no micrograin, no outlines. No baked directional lighting or painted cast shadows; only local albedo variation. Seamlessly match opposite edges in both directions. This is for painting existing solid canopy masses, so opaque full image and no alpha holes. Artwork must remain readable at small gameplay screen size with broad simple colour masses and an elegant quiet brush finish.

prompts: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the supplied game foliage alpha atlas into a TRULY MINIMAL ONE-COLOUR foliage texture. This is an unlit pigment/albedo game asset, not a rendered scene. Preserve the existing EXACT 2x2 layout, four equal quadrant tiles, all four spray shapes, occupied extents, transparency mask, irregular leaf-tipped outer contour, transparent gutters and root positions. Change ONLY the RGB paint inside the existing alpha shapes. Remove ALL of the current alternating light/dark patches. Make every visible leaf shape and the connected interior essentially the SAME restrained sage/moss green, centred on sRGB #748568. All four tiles use that same colour family. Allow only a barely perceptible very broad smooth pigment gradation across each entire spray, maximum about 5 RGB levels lighter/darker; NOT gradients on each little leaf. Most of each shape is almost perfectly uniform. No secondary contrasting patches, no brown stems: any existing stem is the same green. At most one or two tiny low-contrast subtle marks per entire tile, and preferably none. Natural irregular silhouette alone communicates leaves. Beautiful clean minimalist anime-game foliage, flat calm connected colour areas, no vein lines, painted leaf outlines, speckles, mottling, internal high-frequency detail, micrograin, photographic texture, internal patch boundaries, black outlines, yellow-green highlights, dark interior paint, directional illumination, painted cast shadows, AO or baked volume. IMPORTANT: This must look almost like four green silhouette cutouts, not like richly textured leaf clusters.

Precise production correction of the attached ONE-TONE foliage game RGBA atlas. Keep the four quadrant silhouettes and alpha contours in the same places. The interior one muted sage green and extremely gentle broad gradation are already right. REMOVE every thin dark line around all leaf-shaped edges and remove the dark green stem strokes. Fill those pixels with exactly the neighbouring main sage green, including ALL partially opaque anti-alias edge pixels. The RGB of an edge pixel must remain the SAME green as the interior, with no darkened fringe. Alpha alone cuts the silhouette; never draw an outline. No low-alpha speckled coloured residue around the silhouettes: background must be genuinely fully transparent and clean. No veins, stems, tiny marks, dark dots, borders, grain or extra colour. Only a crisp clean alpha silhouette filled with one restrained green family, with barely noticeable smooth broad gradation. Same colour across all four tiles. No per-leaf variation. Do not replace this with a tree render or change the tile layout. Output RGBA with actual transparent background. This will be tiled over hundreds of overlapping 3D planes: even a thin dark border repeats into an ugly dark net, so absolutely NO DARK BORDER, anywhere, including anti-aliased edges. Preserve original approximate opacity extents and proportions.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the supplied game foliage RGBA atlas into a minimalist TWO-CLOSE-COLOUR foliage albedo. Stems must be green in this same palette, no brown third colour. Keep the interior mostly monolithic calm colour, with one or two barely visible broad shape accents at most. Minimalist elegant anime-game foliage, unlit albedo only. No veins, leaf outlines, dark internal patches, fine lines, speckles, dabs, micrograin, photographic noise, yellow highlights, black strokes, painted lighting/shadow/AO/bevel, rendered scene or text. Real transparent background and clean gutters, no checkerboard illustration, no stray pixels or translucent paint outside the existing foliage silhouette. Output square PNG with alpha. The purpose is to reduce colour noise once hundreds of these cards overlap in a 3D canopy.

foliage21_separate_leaf_samples.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: original game foliage RGBA alpha-cutout atlas for an anime-inspired environment in Ember Godot.
Create a clean square 2 by 2 texture atlas, four separate leaf spray tiles, true transparent background, no frame, no text. Each quadrant is a different small spray of discrete simple broadleaf silhouettes: 20 to 28 individually readable oval/tapered pointed leaves. Leaves are arranged coherently in loose fans along imagined branching stems, but DO NOT draw stems or twigs. Tiny groups of 2 or 3 leaves may touch; most leaf silhouettes have clearly transparent space separating them. Keep several bigger irregular channels through each spray. These are separate leaf-shaped spots, NOT one connected green blob with holes punched into it. The entire silhouette must be airy and organically irregular, with leaf shapes also at the outer fringe. Aim for about 35 percent painted area inside each tile's bounding rectangle. Top two tiles moderately grouped, bottom two slightly more open. Use generous clear margins around every tile with no leaf crossing the quadrant boundaries. The fan base/root is near lower-middle of every quadrant, with leaves expanding upward and outward; no foliage at the very bottom 8 percent.
Painting: all leaves use the SAME vivid natural fresh green pigment around sRGB #659f2e, a softly warmer yellow-green variation around #76ac36 near their tops; only a restrained broad smooth gradient within the same colour family, no alternating light/dark random leaves. Minimalist matte flat paint. No veins, flecks, pores, hatching, outlines, speckles, glows, white highlight or shadows baked into artwork. No moss-grey, pastel sage, beige or desaturated olive. Lighting, volume and shadows will be added by the game shader. Smooth crisp opaque leaf interiors and clean alpha edges, real empty transparent spaces between all detached leaf shapes. This is a flat texture asset, NOT a rendered tree, NOT a picture of texture cards, NOT a collage of screenshots. Original artwork guided by the user's examples of simple separate leaf patches and rich green game foliage; do not reproduce proprietary assets.
